newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jardine Group 1996 results unlikely to shine.
newsitem.headline: Jardine Group 1996 results unlikely to shine.

text.p: Jardine Matheson Holdings Ltd is expected to show less than sterling earnings for 1996 when it unveils its results later this week.

Hong Kong-based Jardine Matheson, whose founding is tied up with the birth of the colony, has made no bones of the fact that 1996 was not a good year for it or for holding company Jardine Strategic Holdings Ltd.
Analysts on Tuesday agreed 1996 was not a good year, but added that many of the companies' problems had been resolved.

"We believe the worst is over as the group has now sold its problem assets in Thailand and Australia," said Salomon Brothers analyst Anil Daswani. "We anticipate a recovery in most of its operations over the next two years."
At the heart of the vast Jardine empire, Jardine Matheson holds just under 60 percent in Jardine Strategic, which in turn owns 36 percent of Jardine Matheson.

Jardine Strategic owns 52 percent of retailer Dairy Farm International Holdings Ltd, 23 percent of motor distributor Cycle & Carriage Ltd, 51 percent of hotelier Mandarin Oriental International Ltd and 32 percent of property firm Hongkong Land Holdings Ltd.

Jardine Matheson also owns 75 percent of motor distributor Jardine International Motor Holdings Ltd, 50 percent of securities arm Jardine Fleming, and 100 percent of trading and services group Jardine Pacific.
Looking ahead, however, Daswani said Jardine Pacific's sales of its loss-making Sizzler restaurants in Australia had brightened that unit's prospects.
Following provisions for the troubled Kwik Save Group PLC British supermarket operation in 1996, Dairy Farm was also set to rebound, he added.
But looking back, group members reported a litany of woes.
Dairy Farm was hit by falling profits at Kwik Save and the costs of repositioning its Franklins food concern in Australia.
Unlisted Jardine Pacific was hurt by losses in its Sizzler and Pizza Hut food outlets in Australia, analysts said.
And weak consumption in Hong Kong and Singapore slowed down Jardine International Motor and Cycle & Carriage.
Jardine Matheson in September said its interim net slipped to US$212.5 million from US$257.3 million, and warned its full year trading profit was unlikely to beat the previous year's.
Mike Warren, conglomerates analyst with Morgan Stanley, said the group's activities last year had been marked by writedowns and one-off costs.
One such charge was a US$10 million "hit" as a result of a joint investigation by Hong Kong and British regulators into trading irregularities at Jardine Fleming, he noted.
Salomon's Daswani said he expected Jardine Matheson to post US$405.6 million in net profit including exceptionals, compared with US$420 million in 1995.
Stripping out exceptionals, Jardine Matheson's profits would be US$330.4 million versus US$334 million, he said.
Daswani predicted US$350.4 million in net profits for Jardine Strategic, including exceptionals, up 20.2 percent on 1995. Without exceptionals, it should be US$264.4 million.

Goldman Sachs (Asia) analyst Janice Wallace expected Jardine Matheson to report a net of US$356 million, including exceptionals, in net profits. But minus exceptionals, she predicted Jardine Matheson would post a net of US$320 million.
Results from group members posted so far have been mixed.
Last week, Singapore-based Cycle & Carriage said annual net profits rose to S$200.1 million from S$181.6 million in 1995.
But Hong Kong-based Jardine International Motor said its 1996 net plunged to HK$68.9 million from HK$107.1 million.
